article.title: What’s the Renminbi Got to Do With it?

summary.finding: Predicted the conclusion, the opponent and the rival cause; missed the proof: export timing, the IMF's failed forecasts, and why quotas fall short.

items.label: Is China's export surge just weak home demand, or the weak yuan?
Notes the IMF wrongly forecast a falling surplus, having ignored the currency
Sets the Geneva Report and Beijing against Sobel, Merz and Macron
Treats China's capital controls as given: exporters' dollar sales set the rate
items.note: predicted: real exchange rates move trade, with multi-year lags

items.label: Assumes timing alone separates the yuan's effect from weak demand
items.note: predicted: China's surplus imposes real costs on its partners

items.label: Distrusts China's official balance of payments: repeated method changes hid the surplus
Measures exports against global trade growth, netting out world demand swings
Holds the yuan to Krugman's rule: catching-up economies should appreciate
Shows export growth jumping after the yuan's 2022 fall, outpacing global trade
items.note: predicted: the yuan's slide against the euro and record surpluses

items.label: Cites Mark Sobel on heavy management and Merz and Macron on undervaluation
items.note: predicted: IMF assessments and official Chinese currency data

items.label: Compares the goods surplus in payments data with customs; gap now closed
